meta.name: dolly-legacy-letters
meta.description: Open curated notes on letters, faxes, and song-letters Dolly Parton sent to other performers — short public excerpts only.
meta.thirdPartyNotice: Letter excerpts may remain under separate copyrights. Factual summaries, curation, and metadata are licensed under CC BY 4.0. We do not republish full letters.

letters.summary: A typed thank-you after he helped her Imagination Library at Dollywood — signed, as ever, with I will always love you.
letters.excerpt: I'll always send you a message by pony express… you know how high tech I am!

letters.summary: She still faxes. Miley has to collect them through a lawyer's office. The note was for Mother's Day.
letters.excerpt: How much do I love you? As much as my heart can hold and as far as my arms can reach.

letters.summary: A fax after flowers for the Hannah Montana anniversary — proud to be Aunt Dolly on screen or off.
letters.excerpt: Just know I'm always proud to be your Aunt Dolly.
letters.sourceLabel: The Big 98 / iHeart, citing the Hannah Montana anniversary special

letters.summary: Sometimes the letter is a song. She sat him down and sang the goodbye instead of arguing it.
letters.excerpt: I Will Always Love You — written as a farewell he could hear.

letters.toRole: the voice that carried her song around the world
letters.summary: When The Bodyguard asked for the song, she sent it with one instruction: don't skip the last verse the way Linda Ronstadt had.
letters.excerpt: Be sure and make certain that that last verse can be sung.
